figures.title: Measurement protocol
figures.physical_meaning: Coherent intervals followed by the complete binary Lüders channel.
figures.main_finding: Increasing M shortens each coherent interval without altering the initial state.
figures.axes: Schematic time increases left to right; event spacings are uniform.
figures.limitations: Ideal mathematical projections, no apparatus, ancilla, finite pulse width or detection inefficiency.
figures.suggested_poster_use: Introduce the measurement model; pair with Figure 03.

figures.title: Population evolution
figures.physical_meaning: Resolved populations in the symmetric three-state sector.
figures.main_finding: Measurements of the ground-state sector inhibit excitation even at V=0, where blockade is absent.
figures.axes: Time in microseconds; populations dimensionless, common scales in all panels.
figures.limitations: The Bell population is a coherent projector expectation, not one atom’s excitation probability.
figures.parameters: Common defaults; V=0; M=0,2,10,100; 1001 time samples.

figures.title: Zeno survival curve
figures.physical_meaning: Final ground population and the joint probability of every ground outcome.
figures.main_finding: Both losses approach (T/tau_Z)^2/M; return histories make non-selective population larger at finite M.
figures.axes: Logarithmic measurement count; right panel shows logarithmic loss to resolve near-unity probabilities.
figures.limitations: Exponential shown only at M>=20; asymptotic, not an exact formula for either finite-M curve. M=0 stated separately.
figures.suggested_poster_use: Flagship result; single-column version for narrow spaces.

figures.title: Zeno survival curve
figures.physical_meaning: Final ground population and the joint probability of every ground outcome.
figures.main_finding: Both losses approach (T/tau_Z)^2/M; return histories make non-selective population larger at finite M.
figures.axes: Logarithmic measurement count; right panel shows logarithmic loss to resolve near-unity probabilities.
figures.limitations: Exponential shown only at M>=20; asymptotic, not an exact formula for either finite-M curve. M=0 stated separately.
figures.suggested_poster_use: Flagship result; single-column version for narrow spaces.

figures.title: Short-time quadratic law
figures.physical_meaning: Survival loss of the initial pure state during a single unmeasured interval.
figures.main_finding: The same leading coefficient holds at V/Omega=0 and 100; finite-time corrections need not be the same.
figures.axes: Nanoseconds on a logarithmic x axis; log-log loss at left, loss divided by the leading quadratic term at right.
figures.limitations: Static finite-dimensional Hermitian H makes P(t) even: next correction is O(t^4). tau_Z alone does not fix the useful expansion window.
figures.suggested_poster_use: Explain the mechanism beneath the main survival curve.
figures.parameters: Omega/(2pi)=1 MHz; Delta=phi=0; V/Omega=0,100; t=0.01 to 100 ns; initial |00>.

figures.title: Zeno regime heatmap
figures.physical_meaning: Non-selective ground-state population over total time and measurement count.
figures.main_finding: Sustained protection across the time window requires more measurements as T increases.
figures.axes: Microseconds horizontally, logarithmic M vertically, colour gives final ground population. Amber contour marks 0.95.
figures.limitations: M is a count, not a rate: rate=M/T. Low-M revivals can also yield large final populations; see the matched M=0 panel.
figures.suggested_poster_use: Show the range of useful parameters.
figures.parameters: Omega/(2pi)=1 MHz; Delta=phi=V=0; T=0.01 to 1 us; integer M=1 to 1000; initial |00>.

figures.title: Interaction dependence
figures.physical_meaning: Matched measured and unmeasured endpoints as interaction strength changes.
figures.main_finding: Blockade suppresses |rr> while allowing collective single excitation; ground-sector measurements inhibit excitation even at V=0.
figures.axes: V/Omega dimensionless with a linear segment from 0 to 0.01 then logarithmic; populations at fixed T.
figures.limitations: Endpoint oscillations with V are coherent dynamics, not error bars or a monotonic blockade threshold.
figures.parameters: Common defaults; V/Omega=0 and 0.01 to 100; M=0,10,1000.

figures.title: Density-matrix coherence
figures.physical_meaning: Magnitudes of a physical evolved density matrix before/after the binary Lüders measurement, and magnitudes of removed entries.
figures.main_finding: Ground-to-excited coherences vanish, while all populations and within-Q coherences survive.
figures.axes: Row/column labels are basis indices |00>, |0r>, |r0>, |rr>; all three matrices use one colour scale.
figures.limitations: Magnitude plots do not show phases; complete complex matrices are saved. Not a measurement resolving all four basis states.
figures.parameters: Omega/(2pi)=1 MHz; Delta=phi=V=0; pure |00> evolved for 0.15 us, then one binary measurement.

figures.title: Numerical convergence
figures.physical_meaning: Actual full-density Frobenius errors relative to an independently diagonalised reference.
figures.main_finding: RK4 approaches fourth order; subdividing the exact exponential only changes accumulated floating-point roundoff.
figures.axes: Substeps per coherent interval; dimensionless Frobenius error. Left log-log, right log x and linear error divided by 1e-14.
figures.limitations: RK4 is an additional diagnostic, not the solver used to generate the production figures. Curves are numerical errors, not statistical uncertainties.
figures.parameters: Common defaults; V/Omega=1; M=8; n=1,2,4,8,16,32,64; spectral reference.

figures.title: Measurement-subspace comparison
figures.physical_meaning: Two genuine binary projector choices, with a common ground observable and the population of the sector containing the initial state.
figures.main_finding: Protecting a multidimensional sector permits motion inside it. Avoiding |rr> does not freeze the initial ground state.
figures.axes: Log M; left ground population for both channels, right rank-one P00 or rank-three I-Prr sector population.
figures.limitations: The original any_excitation question only reverses the ground question’s outcomes; it is not an independent dynamics. Rank-three occupancy is not all-success probability.
figures.suggested_poster_use: Explain Zeno dynamics beyond rank-one freezing.
figures.parameters: Common defaults; V=0; ground vs double-excitation binary projectors; M=1 to 10000.
